subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add a core per-agent or grouped foreground command-lane config surface, and what server-controlled capacity contract should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes scheduler isolation, public config, upgrade expectations, and adjacent lane semantics rather than repairing a single broken current contract.

options.title: Design Config-Driven Foreground Lanes
options.body: Add a default-preserving config surface for foreground agent lane selection and per-lane concurrency, with an aggregate safety cap and upgrade tests.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduler RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers design one lane/concurrency model covering foreground agents, hooks, subagents, browser-heavy work, and channel-specific routing.

options.title: Document Separate Gateways
options.body: Decline core foreground lane config for now and document separate gateway instances as the supported isolation pattern.

recommendation.title: Design Config-Driven Foreground Lanes
recommendation.body: Add a default-preserving config surface for foreground agent lane selection and per-lane concurrency, with an aggregate safety cap and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the scheduler/config contract runs through the command-lane enum and centralized concurrency resolver work.
